sentences.text: 2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor in detail.
Perused the case records.

3. In this matter, the prosecution allegation is that in between 02.09.2020 and 04.09.2020, the defacto complainant obtained Rs.1,90,000/- from the husband of the defacto complainant and Rs.2,30,000/- from the friend of the husband of the defacto complainant through their respective accounts maintained at the State Bank of India directly in the account of the 1st accused maintained at Indian Bank, Eruveli, Ernakulam with offer to provide more commission after running business of sale of articles as done by 'Amazon' in Q1 Company.

In this matter, the allegation is that thereafter the 1 st and 2nd accused, sharing common intention, obtained money by offering sale of products of the Company, but there is no business done or the money also not given back.

Accordingly, it is alleged that the accused cheated the defacto complainant and thereby committed offence punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code ('IPC' for short hereinafter).
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners merely introduced the Q1 Company and they did not receive any amount and the amount was deposited by the defacto complainant directly to the Company.

In this regard, they have given emphasis to Annexure A4, a photocopy of a document with title 'enrollment confirmation'.
5.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, since the role of the petitioners is merely that of an introducer and they did not receive any amount directly, offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC would not attract against them.
He also submitted that the Company is not arrayed as an accused in this crime.

6. The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that here the specific allegation against the petitioners is that they had received the money in their account with the offer to give more commission from the account of the defacto complainant and therefore, the other contentions raised by the petitioners are matters to be considered by the trial court during trial.
7.

On perusal of the prosecution allegation, the specific allegation is that in between 02.09.2020 and 04.09.2020, the defacto complainant obtained Rs.1,90,000/- from the husband of the defacto complainant and Rs.2,30,000/- from the friend of the husband of the defacto complainant through their respective accounts maintained at the State Bank of India directly in the account of the 1st accused maintained at Indian Bank, Eruveli, Ernakulam with offer to provide more commission after running business of sale of articles as done by 'Amazon' in Q1 Company.

In this matter, the allegation is that thereafter the 1st and 2nd accused, sharing common intention, obtained money by offering sale of products of the Company, but there is no business done or the money also not given back.
Accordingly, it is alleged that the accused cheated the defacto complainant.

sentences.text: In Annexure A4 also, the sponsor's name is Saranya.
As far as Annexures produced as 4 to 8 are concerned, the same are photocopies and the authenticity of the same can be adjudged only after adducing evidence.
9. Since, prima facie, the materials would show the prosecution allegations warranting trial for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC, quashment sought for cannot be allowed.
10. In the result, this petition stands dismissed.
The interim order granted by this Court on 21.02.2024 stands vacated.
Registry is directed to forward a copy of this order to the trial court for compliance and information.
